messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: array bounds & init checking
parts:
There are two places so far that Stan can seg fault (basically
crash out of C from trying to read memory it shouldn't).

1) using a transformed parameter that has only been declared
but not assigned a value, or

2) using out of bounds array indices.

BUGS solves these problems by:

1) making sure every variable is either sampled (a
parameter for us) or assigned (a transformed parameter
or transformed data) exactly once in the code, and

2) calculating array bounds by running the first iteration
of the model.

At the cost of slowing everything down a bit, I could
implement array-bounds checking and defined checking in
the Stan-GM models.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: array bounds & init checking
parts:
I completely agree.

I'm more thinking of doing it on every loop, though,
so that we can provide some error handling. Given
that we can have expressions in the indices, e.g.,

x[ceil(y)]

and that the value of ceil(y) may change, we really have
to check every time for both bounds and initialization.

- Bob
